entries.sentence: The NHS lists chest pain that feels tight or squeezing, pain that spreads to the arms, neck or jaw, severe breathlessness, pale or grey skin and passing out as reasons to call 999 immediately.

entries.sentence: A heart attack is a medical emergency.

entries.sentence: Not everyone has the classic chest pain.

entries.sentence: NHS 111 Wales notes that women are more likely to have other symptoms such as shortness of breath, feeling or being sick, and back or jaw pain.

entries.sentence: The evidence on differences between men and women is mixed: a study funded by the British Heart Foundation (BHF) found that women having a heart attack reported the same key symptoms as men.

entries.sentence: Other guidance says symptoms can be less typical, particularly in women, older people and people with diabetes.

entries.sentence: The NHS says a heart attack happens when the blood supply to part of the heart is suddenly cut off, so that the heart muscle begins to die.
entries.note: first pass: written from the retrieved search summary text; attributed to the page(s) whose title matches (summaries blend pages)

entries.sentence: Coronary heart disease is the leading cause.
entries.note: first pass: written from the retrieved search summary text; attributed to the page(s) whose title matches (summaries blend pages)

entries.sentence: In coronary heart disease, fatty plaques build up in the coronary arteries, and a plaque can rupture and trigger a clot that blocks the vessel.
entries.note: first pass: written from the retrieved search summary text; attributed to the page(s) whose title matches (summaries blend pages)

entries.sentence: A shortage of oxygen in the blood, for example from carbon monoxide poisoning or lung problems, is a less common cause.
entries.note: first pass: written from the retrieved search summary text; attributed to the page(s) whose title matches (summaries blend pages)

entries.sentence: The NHS lists smoking, high blood pressure, high cholesterol, diabetes, being overweight and a close relative who has had a heart attack among the risk factors.
entries.note: first pass: written from the retrieved search summary text; attributed to the page(s) whose title matches (summaries blend pages)

entries.sentence: Age, sex, family history and ethnicity are factors that cannot be changed.
entries.note: first pass: written from the retrieved search summary text; attributed to the page(s) whose title matches (summaries blend pages)

entries.sentence: A heart attack is a problem with the blood supply to the heart muscle.
entries.note: first pass: written from the retrieved search summary text; attributed to the page(s) whose title matches (summaries blend pages)

entries.sentence: Cardiac arrest is different: the NHS says that if a large part of the heart is damaged, the heart can stop beating altogether.
entries.note: first pass: written from the retrieved search summary text; attributed to the page(s) whose title matches (summaries blend pages)

entries.sentence: The NHS says the main tests for finding out whether someone is having a heart attack are an electrocardiogram (ECG) and blood tests.
entries.note: first pass: written from the retrieved search summary text; attributed to the page(s) whose title matches (summaries blend pages)

entries.sentence: There are two main types.

entries.sentence: In a STEMI, one of the coronary arteries is completely blocked, and the ECG usually shows a rise in a part of the tracing called the ST segment.
entries.note: first pass: written from the retrieved search summary text; attributed to the page(s) whose title matches (summaries blend pages)

entries.sentence: In an NSTEMI, an artery is significantly narrowed rather than fully blocked, and the ECG often shows no abnormality or only subtle changes.
entries.note: first pass: written from the retrieved search summary text; attributed to the page(s) whose title matches (summaries blend pages)

entries.sentence: Damage to the heart muscle lets proteins leak into the blood.
entries.note: first pass: written from the retrieved search summary text; attributed to the page(s) whose title matches (summaries blend pages)

entries.sentence: The most commonly measured is cardiac troponin, and the level helps diagnose the type of heart attack.
entries.note: first pass: written from the retrieved search summary text; attributed to the page(s) whose title matches (summaries blend pages)

entries.sentence: A BHF briefing reports that a high-sensitivity troponin test can double the number of women diagnosed with a heart attack who would otherwise have been told they did not have one.

entries.sentence: Hospital treatment depends on the type and severity of the heart attack.
entries.note: first pass: written from the retrieved search summary text; attributed to the page(s) whose title matches (summaries blend pages)

entries.sentence: The NHS lists clot-dissolving medicine, coronary angioplasty with one or more stents, and coronary artery bypass surgery.
entries.note: first pass: written from the retrieved search summary text; attributed to the page(s) whose title matches (summaries blend pages)

entries.sentence: Angioplasty puts stents into the narrowed or blocked artery to hold it open.
entries.note: first pass: written from the retrieved search summary text; attributed to the page(s) whose title matches (summaries blend pages)

entries.sentence: For a STEMI, the usual approach is to offer a coronary angiogram, which images the arteries, followed by primary percutaneous coronary intervention (primary PCI), meaning emergency angioplasty, when symptoms began recently enough for it to help.
entries.note: first pass: written from the retrieved search summary text; attributed to the page(s) whose title matches (summaries blend pages)

entries.sentence: NICE guideline NG185 covers the early management of acute coronary syndromes.

entries.sentence: The NHS says people usually stay in hospital for about 2 to 5 days after a heart attack, and for 2 or 3 days if they have had angioplasty or stents.

entries.sentence: The most common complications are abnormal heart rhythms (arrhythmias) and heart failure.

entries.sentence: Cardiogenic shock and rupture of the heart muscle are more serious but less common.
entries.note: first pass: written from the retrieved search summary text; attributed to the page(s) whose title matches (summaries blend pages)

entries.sentence: How well someone does depends on age, how much heart muscle was damaged and how quickly treatment began.

entries.sentence: Most people are prescribed several medicines to lower the chance of another heart attack.

entries.sentence: The BHF says antiplatelet drugs such as clopidogrel or ticagrelor are commonly prescribed for a year, and most people are prescribed aspirin for life.

entries.sentence: Beta blockers and statins are also common, and a glyceryl trinitrate spray can ease chest pain.

entries.sentence: The NHS says people are offered cardiac rehabilitation, which can be done in person or remotely.

entries.sentence: The BHF describes it as an exercise and education programme, with expert guidance, exercise sessions and regular assessments.

entries.sentence: It says programmes usually start two to six weeks after leaving hospital and can cover practical matters such as driving, returning to work and holidays.

entries.sentence: The NHS says it can take around 4 to 6 weeks to return to work after a heart attack, and 6 to 8 weeks after a moderate or major one.
